notes: REDEMPTIONS: a stale balance in the picker, and a double count in the closing figure. FIX 1 — THE REDEEM PICKER SHOWED THE SETUP FIGURE, NOT TODAY'S BALANCE. The dropdown read inv.balance, which is the amount typed in at setup and ignores every contribution, growth and lifecycle event since. An FD entered at Rs 1,00,000 and now worth Rs 5,50,000 still offered Rs 1,00,000 while asking how much to redeem — misleading at exactly the moment the number matters. It now shows the projected balance for the current month, net of redemptions already logged (the engine does not model manual redemptions, so those are subtracted here), labelled 'about X now' since it is a projection rather than a statement balance. FIX 2 — A LOGGED REDEMPTION RAISED THE CLOSING BALANCE BY TWICE ITS VALUE. Logged redemptions are folded into totalIncome further up, as the Inflows 'Redemptions' row, because they are new cash entering the spending pool. The closing formula counted income already received as type 'income' only, so a redemption sat inside 'income still to come' while the cash was simultaneously already in the live savings balance. A Rs 1,00,000 redemption therefore moved the close by Rs 2,00,000. Redemptions now count as income already received. Verified: the close moves by exactly the redeemed amount. ANSWERING THE UNDERLYING QUESTION: redeeming into savings needs no special term in the formula. The cash lands in the live balance and is picked up there; the instrument's own balance falls by the same amount, so net worth is unchanged and only the split between cash and investments moves. What it must NOT do is get counted a second time as expected income, which was the defect. BUILDS ON v2026.05.07.07 (per-instrument remaining contributions, so an ad-hoc lump into one instrument can no longer mask an unpaid SIP in another; plus expected redemptions from maturing instruments added to the close). Engine, runProjection and the Decisions tab untouched. No page errors.
